parameters.query:
-- Find-or-create in the database, not in the workflow: two concurrent
-- submits produce one application and both callers get it back.
-- outcome: created | replay | key_conflict | already_open
select * from app.submit_application($1, $2, $3::jsonb, $4, $5);

-- 2xx from the provider: state stays kyc_pending, we only keep its reference.
select $1::uuid as application_id, r.* from app.record_provider_ref($1::uuid, $2) r;

-- Record AND apply in one transaction (keyed on the provider's event_id).
-- If applying fails, nothing is recorded, so the redelivery is processed
-- instead of being dropped as "already seen". Duplicates, lifecycle events,
-- unknown references and stale decisions are all acknowledged with 200 —
-- a decided application has no transition a late callback could take.
select * from app.apply_provider_event($1, $2, $3, $4::bigint, $5::jsonb, $6, $7::app.application_state, $8, $9);

-- SKIP LOCKED keeps concurrent workers off the same rows, and claiming
-- pushes the next attempt out (exponential back-off with jitter). If a pass
-- outlives that lease, the transition keys make a repeat harmless.
select * from app.claim_unknown_applications(25);

-- 2xx from the provider: state stays kyc_pending, we only keep its reference.
select $1::uuid as application_id, r.* from app.record_provider_ref($1::uuid, $2) r;

-- kyc_pending with no provider reference past a 2-minute lease: a new KYC
-- round started by review, or a crash between recording kyc_pending and the
-- provider call. Same round → same idempotency key → the provider de-duplicates.
select * from app.claim_pending_submissions(25, interval '2 minutes');

-- 2xx from the provider: state stays kyc_pending, we only keep its reference.
select $1::uuid as application_id, r.* from app.record_provider_ref($1::uuid, $2) r;
